content_voiceover: This slide compares the major staging and risk stratification systems for multiple myeloma. The classic International Staging System, or ISS, uses only two labs, serum beta-2 microglobulin and albumin, with stage one under three point five and albumin three point five or higher, and stage three at five point five or higher. The Revised ISS adds FISH cytogenetics and LDH, so R-ISS stage three requires ISS stage three plus either a high risk abnormality, del seventeen p, translocation four fourteen, or translocation fourteen sixteen, or an elevated LDH. The newer R2-ISS is a weighted point system folding in ISS stage, LDH, del seventeen p, translocation four fourteen, and one q gain, stratifying patients from low risk at zero points to high risk at three to five points. The IMS-IMWG system focuses on high risk cytogenetics, del seventeen p or T-P-five-three mutation, or combinations of translocations four fourteen, fourteen sixteen, or fourteen twenty co-occurring with one q gain or del one p thirty-two, or a high beta-2 microglobulin with normal creatinine. The bottom table lists additional high risk features for newly diagnosed versus relapsed disease, including extramedullary disease and circulating plasma cells.
keypoints: ISS uses only beta-2 microglobulin and albumin; stage I under 3.5, stage III 5.5 mg/L or more
R-ISS adds FISH (del17p, t4;14, t14;16) and LDH to ISS staging
R2-ISS is a weighted point score combining ISS, LDH, del17p, t4;14, and 1q gain
IMS-IMWG defines high risk by del17p/TP53 mutation or translocations co-occurring with 1q gain or del1p32
Newly diagnosed high-risk features include R-ISS III, extramedullary disease, circulating plasma cells, and high-risk cytogenetics
keypoint_voiceover: Boards love comparing these systems. ISS is just beta-2 microglobulin and albumin. R-ISS layers on FISH cytogenetics and LDH. R2-ISS turns those same variables into a weighted point score. And the newer IMS-IMWG system emphasizes del seventeen p, T-P-five-three mutation, and translocations that co-occur with one q gain or del one p thirty-two as the true high risk drivers, since isolated standard translocations alone carry less prognostic weight than previously thought.
